royaltyEntities.name: PRO Registration (ASCAP or BMI)
royaltyEntities.whyItMatters: Collects songwriter and publisher performance royalties when your music is streamed, broadcast, or performed live.
steps: Choose one PRO (ASCAP or BMI—never register the same songs with both).
Register as a Songwriter first; set up a Publisher entity when you are ready to collect the publisher share of your performance royalties too.
Save your IPI/CAE number—you will need it for split sheets and The MLC.

royaltyEntities.name: The MLC (Mechanical Licensing Collective)
royaltyEntities.whyItMatters: Collects U.S. digital audio mechanical royalties from Spotify, Apple Music, and DSPs that your distributor does NOT collect.
steps: Create a free Member account at themlc.com.
Connect your PRO IPI number and claim your catalog using your ISRC/ISWC codes.

royaltyEntities.name: SoundExchange
royaltyEntities.whyItMatters: Collects neighboring rights / digital performance royalties from Pandora, SiriusXM, and webcasters.
steps: Register as both Featured Artist and Sound Recording Copyright Owner (if independent).
Submit your ISRCs to claim historical and ongoing royalties.

royaltyEntities.name: DSP Artist Profiles (Spotify & Apple Music)
royaltyEntities.whyItMatters: Required to pitch unreleased music to editorial playlists and customize your artist profile.
steps: Claim your profile immediately after uploading your first release to your distributor.
Pitch unreleased tracks as early as you can, ideally 3 to 4 weeks before release day.

releaseMilestones.label: Finalize 24-bit WAV masters, 3000x3000px cover art, and lyrics
Upload to distributor & lock in ISRC/UPC codes
Submit your editorial pitch (Spotify for Artists, Amazon Music): earlier is better, and it must be before release day
Register song splits with PRO (ASCAP/BMI) and The MLC
Launch pre-save link, finalize EPK, and schedule teaser clips
Release Day: Submit ISRCs to SoundExchange & push primary CTA
